Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official online portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

The foreign shareholders incorporate the SL before a Spanish notary and register it at the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil). The SL then must apply to AEAT for its definitive tax identification number (NIF) by filing the official census declaration (Form 036) within six months of obtaining the provisional NIF at incorporation. The same Form 036 simultaneously registers the company in the Spanish VAT census (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) and yields the Spanish IVA identification number, which is the NIF with the ES prefix for intra-EU transactions. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment in Spain obtain only a non-resident NIF (Form 030) where needed for withholding or Spanish VAT obligations.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — an SL is a separate corporate taxpayer subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on its worldwide income; it is not eligible for any pass-through tax classification and does not qualify for transparent treatment under Spanish domestic law. — The foreign shareholders incorporate the SL before a Spanish notary and register it at the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil). The SL then must apply to AEAT for its definitive tax identification number (NIF) by filing the official census declaration (Form 036) within six months of obtaining the provisional NIF at incorporation. The same Form 036 simultaneously registers the company in the Spanish VAT census (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) and yields the Spanish IVA identification number, which is the NIF with the ES prefix for intra-EU transactions. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment in Spain obtain only a non-resident NIF (Form 030) where needed for withholding or Spanish VAT obligations.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — an SL is a separate corporate taxpayer subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on its worldwide income; it is not eligible for any pass-through tax classification and does not qualify for transparent treatment under Spanish domestic law.

Available election forms

No check-the-box or U.S.-style entity classification elections are available. Elective Spanish regimes applicable to an SL include: (i) the reduced 15% Corporate Income Tax rate for newly constituted entities engaging in an economic activity in their first two tax periods (Art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014, LIS); (ii) fiscal consolidation for qualifying groups where the parent holds at least 75% directly or indirectly in the SL (50% for listed companies), under Arts. 62–96 LIS; (iii) the ETVE holding-company regime election for Spanish-resident entities whose main purpose is the management of foreign shareholdings; (iv) the optional cash-basis VAT scheme (Criterio de Caja) for operators whose annual turnover is below EUR 2,000,000. Hybrid mismatch rules transposing ATAD (Law 4/2019) are mandatory and non-elective.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR — Spain imposes no general de minimis turnover threshold: any person habitually supplying taxable goods or services in the course of business must register as an IVA operator before commencing activity. The only contextual thresholds are (i) EUR 10,000 in annual cross-border intra-EU distance sales of goods triggering Spanish VAT obligations, and (ii) EUR 2,000,000 in turnover for eligibility for the optional cash-basis VAT scheme.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Goods: supplies of tangible personal property, including sterile examination nitrile gloves, physically dispatched or transported by the seller, the non-EU purchaser, or a carrier from Spanish customs territory to a non-EU destination qualify for VAT exemption with deduction of input VAT (effective 0%) under Art. 21 of Law 37/1992, provided the goods depart the EU within the statutory export time window, generally evidenced within three months of dispatch, and within 90 days where the shipment control procedure is used. Services: B2B services rendered to non-EU entrepreneurs fall outside the taxable scope of Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rules of Art. 69 LIVA and are therefore subject to effective 0% Spanish taxation, with input VAT recovered through the deduction or refund channels.

  • Single Administrative Document (DUA) / Spanish Customs Export Declaration lodged and validated in the AES with an issued Movement Reference Number (MRN).
  • Commercial invoice and detailed packing list containing ISIC 3250 product codes, description of the sterile synthetic nitrile gloves, batch numbers, quantities, and Incoterms.
  • Transport document — Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note — evidencing physical dispatch from Spanish customs territory to the final non-EU destination.
  • The salida certificate (certificado de salida) or other electronic customs proof confirming that the goods physically departed the EU customs territory.
  • Bank payment evidence via the mandated payment rails (SWIFT LC or TT Wire) demonstrating receipt of export proceeds, including the inward remittance reference.
  • Where preferential origin is claimed, the Certificate of Origin (EUR.1 or Form A), together with any mandatory sanitary or CE compliance certificates required for medical device PPE export clearance.

Mandatory structured B2B e-invoicing applies under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece): suppliers must issue electronic invoices in the accredited interoperable Facturae XML profile through certified private platforms or the AEAT facade, and recipients must be able to receive such invoices. The Veri*factu regime (Royal Decree 1007/2023) requires business software in cash-handling activities to create a hash-chained record of transactional invoices accessible to AEAT on demand, with QR-code or Digital Identification control; there is no continuous real-time VAT fiscal clearance for ordinary B2B exports, but customs movements require electronic lodging in the Spanish Automated Export System (AES) and clearance must be evidenced by the Movement Reference Number (MRN).

AEAT may deny the zero-rating claim where export documentation is missing, materially defective, or untimely, and will re-assess the supply at the standard 21% VAT rate with late-payment interest. The four-year statute of limitation allows retrospective clawback of previously zero-rated or refunded VAT. Administrative penalties under Arts. 191–193 LGT range from 50% to 150% of the tax loss, with the highest range applied where the false export documentation derives from concealment or simulated operations. Where the intentionally concealed VAT exceeds EUR 120,000 in one tax period, or EUR 120,000 over four years, criminal tax fraud liability arises under Arts. 305–305 bis of the Criminal Code, and the legal representatives, directors, and customs-declaring brokers may incur joint and several liability in addition to public publication of the sanction.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a full member of the European Union and the euro area. The euro is freely convertible, and Spain applies the EU principle of unrestricted movement of capital. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully liberalised for residents and non-residents. Profit remittances from a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) may be freely repatriated after corporate income tax compliance, subject only to standard withholding on dividends for non-resident shareholders, anti-money laundering due diligence by the paying bank, and statistical declaration to the DGTOE where thresholds apply. The manufacture and export of sterile examination nitrile gloves (ISIC 3250 / NAICS 339113) is not subject to any sectoral exchange restriction. Spanish banks generally convert EUR/USD and other major currencies at market rates, but availability for exotic currencies may be more limited.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There are no mandatory export-proceeds surrender rules in Spain. Exporters are not required to convert foreign-currency receipts into EUR nor to repatriate them within a specified statutory timeline. Export receipts may be held in foreign currency, converted freely, or used directly to pay foreign suppliers, subject to internal corporate treasury policy and Spanish balance-of-payments reporting obligations. Under Spanish foreign exchange regulations, export and import transactions above the applicable reporting threshold (currently EUR 1.25 million or its equivalent for annual aggregate settlements, with certain statistical forms such as D-6 and continuous monthly reporting) must be declared to the DGTOE for statistical purposes. The declaration is informational only and does not constitute an exchange-control requirement.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), functioning as the Spanish national central bank and banking supervisor, together with the Dirección General de Transacciones y Operaciones Exteriores (DGTOE) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, which administers Spanish foreign exchange, foreign investment and balance-of-payments reporting under the Royal Decree 1816/1991 and its subsequent amendments.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Airwallex Fit: High

Medium-High for operational Euro-denominated collections and outbound wires, but Low for serving as the primary capital-escrow depository. A Spanish SL may lawfully use EEA-authorised e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions under the E-Money Directive and PSD2, provided the institution holds a valid authorisation in an EU/EEA member state or has been passported into Spain. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise Business, Payoneer, and Airwallex can be used for trade settlements, supplier disbursements, and foreign-currency conversion, but they are generally not accepted by Spanish notaries for the certification of capital contributions in an SL. The constitutional deed for the SL requires a bank certificate of capital deposit issued by a credit institution located in the EU/EEA that is a bank, not merely an EMI. Legal constraints include: EMI safeguarding requirements, restrictions on providing credit, data residency and AML/CFT obligations, and the need for the EMI's Spanish or passporting licence to be verified before account opening.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident shareholders and foreign beneficial owners with no prior EU banking footprint attracting enhanced due diligence and possible rejection if UBO documentation is incomplete or not apostilled.

Root cause: Non-resident shareholders and foreign beneficial owners with no prior EU banking footprint attracting enhanced due diligence and possible rejection if UBO documentation is incomplete or not apostilled.

Defense evidence: Provide a certified copy of the constitutional deed (escritura pública) registered in the Mercantile Registry, the NIF (CIF) tax certificate, a current certificate of the beneficial ownership registry (Registro de Titularidades Reales), apostilled and legalised passport copies of all direct and indirect shareholders, a clear corporate organigram, and bank references from the home jurisdiction. For Spanish SLs, the initial EUR 3,000 (or agreed) capital contribution certificate issued by the Spanish bank is also mandatory.
Expected pattern of high volumes of cross-border TT/LC transactions, or frequent payments to third-party suppliers in multiple jurisdictions, which may be flagged as a mismatch against the declared, low-risk medical PPE activity.

Root cause: Expected pattern of high volumes of cross-border TT/LC transactions, or frequent payments to third-party suppliers in multiple jurisdictions, which may be flagged as a mismatch against the declared, low-risk medical PPE activity.

Defense evidence: Submit a detailed business plan and treasury forecast showing the trade flow: selected supplier invoices, pro-forma invoices, purchase orders, contracts with overseas distributors, ISO 13485 and CE-marking certificates, EORI number, and the ISIC/NAICS classification of the product. Maintain a historical ledger of past export transactions, a documented AML/CFT risk assessment, and clear internal controls on third-party payment approvals.
Payments to or from jurisdictions with enhanced risk, including Latin American and Middle Eastern markets that the Spain-Latin America trade corridor may target, triggering temporary freezes and request for comprehensive end-to-end beneficial owner verification.

Root cause: Payments to or from jurisdictions with enhanced risk, including Latin American and Middle Eastern markets that the Spain-Latin America trade corridor may target, triggering temporary freezes and request for comprehensive end-to-end beneficial owner verification.

Defense evidence: Build and present the complete end-to-end transaction chain: contract in Spanish/English, market registration certificate for the glove product, commercial licence for imported medical devices, UNSPSC or HS code (e.g., 3926.20 or 4015.19 depending on material), import licences from the destination country, sanctions screening evidence for all counterparties, and an explanation of freight, insurance, and each payment purpose code. If the counterparty has no credit institution rating, add invoices from freight forwarders and logistics providers to substantiate the physical trade.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

For an SL capital contribution, funds must be transferred by Swift MT103 or through an express domestic/SEPA transfer from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's new bank account, referencing the notarial deed of incorporation or capital increase, the shareholder's name, and the capital subscription records. The bank must issue a certificate of deposit confirming receipt of the statutory capital (desembolso) which the notary attaches to the deed. For non-EU foreign investment, after the notarial deed is granted, the SL (or its notary) must file the annual or transactional foreign-investment declaration with the DGTOE under Royal Decree 571/2020. The recommended wire purpose code is 'GITI/CIP' (Cross-Border Capital Injection / Foreign Direct Investment) using ISO 20022 purpose codes such as 'FDI1' or 'CAPD', with the narrative clearly stating 'Direct foreign investment in ordinary capital of Spanish SL'. The bank may request a copy of the signed share subscription, passport of the transferor, and source-of-funds evidence; the wire should originate only from the shareholder's own bank account and not a third-party pooling account.For trade settlements related to nitrile glove production inputs and export logistics, Spanish SLs use: (i) the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) immediate rail for EUR payments to EU suppliers; (ii) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for non-EUR or non-EU payments, with purpose codes such as 'TRADE' / 'ADVA' for advance payments, and reference to the underlying commercial invoice; (iii) SWIFT MT700 commercial letters of credit for high-value or high-risk jurisdictions, where the Spanish issuing bank adds an irrevocable deferred-payment LC; and (iv) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for established buyer relationships. Each outbound payment must be supported by the supplier invoice, purchase order, transport documents or Bill of Lading where dispatched, and the relevant DGTOE reporting if the cumulative transaction exceeds EUR 1.25 million. No separate central bank authorisation is required, but the bank must screen counterparties for EU sanctions.Contractual forward ( outright EUR/USD FX forward with a Spanish credit institution or EU-licensed investment firm)Rolling or window forward contracts for EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL or EUR/CLP where the underlying Latin American trade receivable/payable is demonstratedNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offered by Spanish banks for illiquid emerging-market currencies that are not freely transferable or where deliverability is limitedFX swaps (short-dated exchange of EUR and foreign currency with a simultaneous reversal)Cross-currency swaps involving EUR and USD/Latin American currencies for medium-term matching of cross-border cash flowsPlain-vanilla over-the-counter FX options (with premium payment) that are economically-linked to specific export invoices or capital flows

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium-High for operational Euro-denominated collections and outbound wires, but Low for serving as the primary capital-escrow depository. A Spanish SL may lawfully use EEA-authorised e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions under the E-Money Directive and PSD2, provided the institution holds a valid authorisation in an EU/EEA member state or has been passported into Spain. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise Business, Payoneer, and Airwallex can be used for trade settlements, supplier disbursements, and foreign-currency conversion, but they are generally not accepted by Spanish notaries for the certification of capital contributions in an SL. The constitutional deed for the SL requires a bank certificate of capital deposit issued by a credit institution located in the EU/EEA that is a bank, not merely an EMI. Legal constraints include: EMI safeguarding requirements, restrictions on providing credit, data residency and AML/CFT obligations, and the need for the EMI's Spanish or passporting licence to be verified before account opening.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

24% general rate under Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) for dividends paid to non-residents without a permanent establishment in Spain; 19% for EU/EEA residents under the general EU/EEA rule where not exempted; 0% for qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive dividends, subject to holding and substance conditions; treaty rates may reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on the relevant double-taxation agreement.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

The Modelo 200 annual return must be filed within 25 days after the six-month period following the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year entity, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 001 - NIF/identification Tax Identification Number of the tax entity, legal form code, dominant group indicator, and main corporate identification data. Non-resident companies acting through a Spanish permanent establishment must obtain an NIF-N and include the branch's local tax identity; non-resident entities without a permanent establishment do not file Modelo 200. Late filing of Modelo 200 without prior AEAT demand is subject to a graduated surcharge under Article 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months, and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT formally requires the return, the penalty may be a proportional fine of 50% to 150% of the tax loss. Employer withholding and quarterly Modelo 202 failures attract additional fixed penalties and daily surcharges. Where deliberate evasion exceeds EUR 120,000 in any tax period, criminal tax fraud proceedings may be instituted.
Box 520 - Accounting result Pre-tax accounting profit or loss of the Spanish company prepared under Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC). For a non-resident with a permanent establishment, enter the accounting result derived from audio-separated Spanish-branch accounts; passive foreign income not attributable to the Spanish PE should be excluded. Late filing of Modelo 200 without prior AEAT demand is subject to a graduated surcharge under Article 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months, and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. Box 522 - Permanent and temporary differences Adjustments to accounting result to arrive at taxable base, including reversal of temporary differences, permanent adjustments, and prior-year tax loss offset. Non-resident PEs must apply the same adjustments as resident companies, but reconciliation should reflect only assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses economically connected to the Spanish PE. Employer withholding and quarterly Modelo 202 failures attract additional fixed penalties and daily surcharges. Where deliberate evasion exceeds EUR 120,000 in any tax period, criminal tax fraud proceedings may be instituted.
Box 557 - Taxable base Taxable base after integration of qualifying capitalization reserve and compensation of prior tax losses. For a Spanish PE, the taxable base is the net income effectively connected to the PE determined under Article 13 of the Non-Resident Income Tax Act; deductions such as the capitalization reserve require Spanish substance. Late filing of Modelo 200 without prior AEAT demand is subject to a graduated surcharge under Article 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months, and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT formally requires the return, the penalty may be a proportional fine of 50% to 150% of the tax loss. Employer withholding and quarterly Modelo 202 failures attract additional fixed penalties and daily surcharges. Where deliberate evasion exceeds EUR 120,000 in any tax period, criminal tax fraud proceedings may be instituted.
Box 580 - Applicable tax rate Corporate income tax rate applied to the taxable base: generally 25%; 15% for qualifying newly created entities within the limits explained above. Non-resident PEs generally use the same 25% statutory rate. Treaty nondiscrimination clauses do not ordinarily alter the rate, but income tax treaty rules may affect the computation of business profits. Employer withholding and quarterly Modelo 202 failures attract additional fixed penalties and daily surcharges. Box 584 - Gross tax payable (cuota íntegra) Result of applying the tax rate to the taxable base before deductions, bonuses, and double-taxation relief. Non-resident PEs include credits for taxes withheld at source in Spain and foreign income taxes attributable to the PE when they qualify for double-taxation relief under the relevant tax treaty. Late filing of Modelo 200 without prior AEAT demand is subject to a graduated surcharge under Article 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months, and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. Box 618 - Deductions and tax reliefs R&D credit, patent box, environmental investment credit, export credit, and other legally recognized tax incentives. Only incentives available to a Spanish PE under domestic law may be claimed; they must be substantiated by Spanish bookkeeping and by the PE's actual execution of the qualifying activities. Box 628 - Differential tax payable/refundable Final tax result after offsetting Modelo 202 installment payments, withholding taxes, and other payments on account made during the tax period. Non-resident PEs settle any residual balance through the annual Modelo 200 and may not offset taxes already paid abroad except where permitted by the applicable DTA and domestic double-tax relief provisions. Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 10,000,000

Economic substance scope: Spain does not maintain offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations comparable to low-tax jurisdictions. However, Spanish tax law imposes a real economic substance doctrine through Article 15 of the General Tax Law (simulation), Article 13 of the Corporate Income Tax Act (attribution of dependent enterprise profits to a PE), the controlled foreign company regime, and the OECD Treaty Abuse Limitation / Principal Purpose Test. A Spanish SL lacking physical premises, qualified personnel, management decision-making, or business risk in Spain may be recharacterized as a shell entity, with consequent denial of treaty benefits, disregarding of artificial intercompany arrangements, and reallocation of business profits to the real economic owner.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and intentional omission of income

Statutory sanction: Proportional tax penalty between 50% and 150% of the evaded tax amount plus late-payment interest. Criminal tax fraud is triggered when defrauded tax amounts exceed EUR 120,000 per tax period, punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.

Director personal liability: Directors and legal representatives who ordered or participated in the infringement are jointly and severally liable for the defrauded tax and penalties; criminal conviction may add travel bans, seizure of personal assets, disqualification from public contracts, and custodial sentences.
Artificial shell company and simulation of corporate activity

Statutory sanction: Recharacterization under Article 15 LGT as simulated transactions, denial of treaty benefits, CFC attribution of passive income to the Spanish entity, 25% corporate income tax assessment plus penalties, and financial interst on unpaid tax. Qualified offshore shell companies may also be reached under EU anti-tax-avoidance directives.

Director personal liability: Directors' personal liability may arise under the 'levantamiento del velo' doctrine, including joint liability for taxes and penalties, civil restitution, prohibition on leaving Spanish territory pending proceedings, and, in cases of fraud, criminal liability for tax evasion.
Transfer pricing mispricing and inadequate documentation

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may adjust the transaction to arm's length, increasing Spanish taxable base, impose a 15% penalty on the amount of the secondary adjustment, apply late-payment interest, and levy an additional 50% to 150% proportional penalty if the TP adjustment arises from intentional falsity or manipulation.

Director personal liability: Directors who approved or knowingly participated in the transfer pricing mispricing are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax, penalties, and interest; may also be held personally liable for damages to the company and charged with tax fraud if the adjustment reveals criminal culpability.
AML, cash-structuring, and cross-border payment red flags

Statutory sanction: Violations of Law 10/2010 on prevention of money laundering can result in administrative fines from EUR 60,000 to EUR 5,000,000 for serious or very serious infringements, and may include temporary closure of the business and loss of operating licenses. Criminal money laundering charges can be pursued if proceeds arise from predicate crime.

Director personal liability: Legal representatives and AML compliance officers may be personally fined, prohibited from management roles, ordered to travel bans, and, where criminal laundering is proven, subjected to imprisonment. The corporate veil is pierced where the company was used as a mere instrument to execute fraudulent transactions.
